newsitem.title: USA: Kaczynski must give writing samples, judge says.
newsitem.headline: Kaczynski must give writing samples, judge says.

text.p: A federal judge, brushing aside defence objections, has ruled that Unabomber suspect Theodore Kaczynski must provide handwriting samples for prosecutors, court documents showed Thursday.
Prosecutors believe the samples will help them show that Kaczynski wrote documents found at his tiny Montana cabin, including diaries they say contained his "detailed admission" to 16 bomb attacks.

Kaczynski, a 54-year-old former mathematics professor, is accused of being the shadowy Unabomber, who killed three people and injured 23 during an anti-technology bombing campaign between 1978 and 1995.
Kaczynski, arrested in Montana a year ago, has pleaded not guilty to Sacramento charges accusing him of four bomb attacks, two fatal.
Last month, U.S. Magistrate Gregory Hollows ordered Kaczynski to provide handwriting samples for prosecutors.
Defence lawyers asked U.S. District Judge Garland Burrell, the judge in charge of the Kaczynski case in Sacramento, to reconsider Hollows' order.
They maintained the court lacked authority to order Kaczynski to provide handwriting samples and that the government failed to show its request was reasonable or that it needed the samples.
In an order dated Wednesday, Burrell upheld the magistrate's order, saying the defence had failed to show that his findings were wrong.
In his order last month, Hollows ordered Kaczynski to provide the handwriting samples within 30 days at the Sacramento County Jail where he is being held.
He said a government expert would give Kaczynski typed phrases and Kaczynski would be told to reproduce them "in his own, undisguised handwriting or handprinting as requested."

Hollows said the government would be given no more than three sessions to obtain the samples. No session could last more than two hours and all three together could not last more than five hours, he said.

Defence lawyers have conceded Kaczynski wrote more than 800 pages of documents, mainly letters to his mother Wanda and brother David, that the government has also obtained. They said these could be used for comparison by the government's handwriting expert.
Investigators found handwritten and handprinted documents at Kaczynski's cabin, written in English, Spanish and numeric code, according to court documents.
Prosecutor Robert Cleary said in court last September that Kaczynski's handwritten diary contained phrases such as "I mailed that bomb" or "I sent that bomb."

According to news reports, investigators also found at the cabin bomb components, an original copy of the Unabomber's rambling, 35,000-word anti-technology manifesto sent to newspapers in 1995 and a typewriter used to type it.
Kaczynski is due to go on trial in Sacramento in November.
